title: Design a Rate Limiter
relevance: High — the canonical Strategy + concurrency LLD / machine-coding problem (campus + experienced); Uber, Stripe, Amazon, Google, Meta, Atlassian, Flipkart, and API-platform loops use it to probe algorithm choice, OCP, per-key locking, and the bridge to distributed Redis.
company_notes: Campus/new-grad machine-coding or LLD (India and FAANG-style): often implement Token Bucket plus one other algorithm with Strategy + concurrency. SDE-2+ keeps the same OOP surface with harder probes—per-key locking, injectable Clock/Store, Redis Lua stretch, fail-open, header contract, algorithm choice by traffic shape (Stripe/Uber/Amazon/Meta/Google, API gateway teams). Sibling of HLD hq02 and foundation h09; high-frequency systems-flavored LLD alongside LRU cache and logger.

phases.goal: Clarify in-memory LLD scope, mandatory allow/deny contract, multi-algorithm FR, and what stays HLD stretch.

must_hit.point: Scope as single-process in-memory LLD (classes, Strategy, per-key state, thread-safety, Factory) unless told otherwise; Redis / multi-DC / fail-open are stretch, not built mid-round unless asked.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States single JVM in-memory default and names gateway/Redis/fail-open as HLD stretch distinct from hq02.

must_hit.point: Mandatory FR: given identity key (often plus endpoint), allow/deny under a configured rule; support at least two algorithms behind one interface; return remaining quota and a retry hint on deny.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Lists key(+endpoint), rule-based allow/deny, ≥2 strategies, remaining + retryAfter on deny.

must_hit.point: Result contract is RateLimitResult {allowed, remaining, retryAfterMs} (retryAfterMs null when allowed), mapping to HTTP 429 + Retry-After / X-RateLimit-* when asked.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names allowed/remaining/retryAfterMs and ties deny to 429 + Retry-After headers.

must_hit.point: NFR: correct under concurrent checks; low latency in-process; extensible algorithms and storage; deterministic tests via injectable Clock.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Calls out concurrency correctness, latency, OCP for algos/store, and FakeClock for tests.

must_hit.point: Common extensions to ask first: per-tier limits (free/pro), multi-permit cost, default rule for unknown endpoints, admin hot-update of rules.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Proactively asks about tiers, permit costs, default endpoint rule, and admin rule updates.

probes: Is this in-memory single process or distributed, and what does allow() return beyond a boolean?
Which algorithms are mandatory in v1, and is the key user, IP, API key, or (clientId, endpoint)?

hints.1: Ask process vs distributed and bool vs rich result before drawing classes.
hints.2: Separate mandatory FR (key, multi-algo interface, remaining/retry) from tier/multi-permit extensions.
hints.3: State: single JVM; allow(clientId, endpoint) → {allowed, remaining, retryAfterMs}; ≥2 algorithms behind Strategy; Clock injectable; Redis as stretch.

phases.goal: Name the core domain objects: facade, strategy, config/rule, result, and per-key state store.

must_hit.point: RateLimitConfig / RateLimitRule carries limit, window/rate, capacity, refill rate, and algorithm type for an endpoint.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Describes a config/rule object with those fields rather than hardcoding rates in the facade.

must_hit.point: RateLimitResult holds allowed, remaining, and retryAfterMs (null if allowed).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Shows a result type with those three fields returned from allow().

must_hit.point: Per-key state is keyed by identity such as composite "userId:endpoint" (or API key) so policies can differ per route; unknown endpoints can fall back to a default config.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names composite keying and default config for unknown endpoints.

must_hit.point: Optional LimitResolver selects tiered quotas (free vs pro) from plan/config rather than hardcoding rates inside the strategy.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Mentions a resolver or per-plan config sitting above the strategy math.

probes: What fields belong on RateLimitConfig and RateLimitResult?
How do you key per-client state so /search and /login can have different policies?

hints.1: Think config/rule, result DTO, and a map of per-key buckets—not only a boolean.
hints.2: Composite clientId:endpoint key; config map by endpoint; optional LimitResolver for tiers.

phases.goal: Sketch RateLimiter facade, RateLimitAlgorithm Strategy hierarchy, Factory, and DIP for Clock/Store.

must_hit.point: RateLimiter facade resolves endpoint config, gets/creates per-key algorithm state, delegates allow, and returns RateLimitResult—callers never switch on algorithm type.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Draws facade orchestration: config lookup → per-key strategy/state → allow → result.

must_hit.point: RateLimitAlgorithm / RateLimitStrategy interface with concrete TokenBucket, FixedWindow, SlidingWindowLog, SlidingWindowCounter, and LeakyBucket—Strategy swaps algos without editing the facade.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Shows interface plus multiple concrete strategies; facade depends on the abstraction.

must_hit.point: LimiterFactory maps config algorithm string/enum plus algoConfig to a concrete strategy instance (Factory Method).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Factory branch from "TokenBucket" (etc.) + algoConfig creates the right class.

must_hit.point: DIP: inject Clock (SystemClock / FakeClock) and optional Storage (InMemoryStore ConcurrentHashMap / RedisStore stretch); avoid cargo-cult Singleton on the limiter.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Constructor-injects Clock and Store; FakeClock for tests; Redis behind Storage only as stretch.

probes: Which patterns does this problem exist to test, and where does each sit in the diagram?
How does the facade stay closed when you add Sliding Window Counter tomorrow?

hints.1: Name Strategy and Factory before coding concrete buckets.
hints.2: Facade → Factory + config map + per-key strategy/state; Clock/Store injected.
hints.3: RateLimiter uses LimiterFactory and RateLimitAlgorithm; TokenBucket…LeakyBucket implement the interface; Storage/Clock abstractions for DIP.

phases.goal: Verbalize algorithm tradeoffs, implement lazy-refill Token Bucket (and a second algo) with O(1) hot path where claimed.

must_hit.point: Token Bucket: capacity and refill rate; lazy refill on each request as tokens += elapsed * rate capped at capacity—no background refill thread; controlled bursts; O(1); industry default.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Explains lazy refill formula, burst allowance, O(1), and rejects a timer refill thread for the interview default.

must_hit.point: Algorithm cheat-sheet: Fixed window is simple but has 2× burst at boundary; Sliding window log is accurate but O(n) memory; Sliding window counter is approximate ~O(1); Leaky bucket smooths with constant drain / no burst out.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Contrasts fixed-window boundary spike, log memory, counter approximation, and leaky smoothness vs token bucket.

must_hit.point: Store per-key state in ConcurrentHashMap via computeIfAbsent for cold keys; hot path is one key’s allow() and must stay O(1) for token/fixed/sliding-counter—do not scan all keys.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Uses ConcurrentHashMap.computeIfAbsent; argues O(1) allow for those algos and sparse seen-key storage.

must_hit.point: Factory/config shape includes endpoint, algorithm string, and algoConfig such as capacity and refillRatePerSecond; optional idle-key TTL/eviction for memory follow-up.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Shows JSON-like config driving Factory and mentions TTL/eviction for idle clients.

probes: Walk through Token Bucket allow() including when tokens refill—do you need a background thread?
Why might Fixed Window allow a 2× burst, and when would you pick Sliding Log instead of Token Bucket?

hints.1: Lazy refill on the request path is the interview default.
hints.2: Compare fixed-window boundary spike, log O(n) memory, and token-bucket O(1) bursts.
hints.3: tokens += elapsed * rate capped at capacity; ConcurrentHashMap.computeIfAbsent; Fixed Window 2× boundary; Sliding Log accurate but O(n).

phases.goal: Show OCP for new algorithms and DIP so storage/clock can change without rewriting the facade.

must_hit.point: Add a new algorithm = new RateLimitAlgorithm class plus one Factory branch; zero edits to RateLimiter call sites (OCP).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Adds a class + Factory case; facade and callers stay unchanged.

must_hit.point: SRP split: strategy owns rate math, store owns persistence, facade owns orchestration; depend on RateLimitAlgorithm / Storage / Clock abstractions (DIP).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Assigns math/persistence/orchestration to separate types and names the injected abstractions.

must_hit.point: Storage interface enables InMemoryStore today and RedisStore later; tiered limits via LimitResolver/config per plan—not hardcoded rates inside strategies.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Shows Storage swap path and plan-based LimitResolver for free vs pro.

probes: How do you add Sliding Window Counter without editing RateLimiter callers?
Where would Redis or FakeClock plug in without rewriting strategies?

hints.1: OCP means new class + Factory branch, not a growing facade switch of math.
hints.2: Strategy math, Store persistence, Facade orchestration; inject Clock/Store.
hints.3: New algorithm class + Factory branch; Storage/Clock DIP; LimitResolver for tiers.

phases.goal: Eliminate check-then-consume races with per-key locking (or CAS), not one global lock on the map.

must_hit.point: Check-then-consume is a race: two threads with one token left can both be allowed on naive read-modify-write—prefer per-key lock / synchronized on the bucket object, or AtomicReference+CAS / Redis Lua for distributed.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names the double-allow race and fixes it with per-bucket sync, CAS, or Lua—not unlocked read-then-write.

must_hit.point: Never one global lock on the whole map/facade under load: ConcurrentHashMap.computeIfAbsent for cold keys, then lock the bucket not the map; global synchronized allow() is correct but serializes unrelated users.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Rejects facade-wide lock as the senior answer; locks per key after computeIfAbsent.

must_hit.point: Distributed across N pods: shared Redis with atomic Lua for token-bucket check-and-consume; local in-memory under-enforces by replica count; fail-open vs fail-closed is a product call.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Escalates to Redis+Lua atomicity, replica under-enforcement, and fail-open/closed tradeoff.

probes: Two threads, one token left—both allowed? Where is the race and how do you fix it?
Is synchronized on the whole RateLimiter enough, and what changes for multiple pods?

hints.1: The bug is read-modify-write on tokens, not missing a concurrent map.
hints.2: Lock or CAS the per-key bucket; computeIfAbsent then synchronize the bucket.
hints.3: Per-key lock/CAS; avoid global facade lock; Redis Lua for multi-instance; mention fail-open/closed.

tradeoffs.strong_answer: A switch compiles faster in a timebox, but Strategy + Factory is the expected OCP answer for adding Sliding Window Counter tomorrow without editing callers.
Token Bucket allows controlled bursts with O(1) memory; Sliding Log is exact but memory grows with request rate—pick consciously for the traffic shape.
synchronized allow() on the facade is correct but serializes unrelated users; locking the per-key bucket (or CAS) is the senior concurrency signal.
Background refill timers add complexity and races; lazy refill on each request (tokens += elapsed * rate capped at capacity) is the interview default.
Local memory under-enforces by replica count; Redis + Lua gives atomic check-and-consume across instances; fail-open vs fail-closed is a product call (Stripe often fail-open for request limiters).

gotchas.trap: Two threads see one token left and both are allowed.
gotchas.correction: Race on read-modify-write—use per-key lock, CAS, or Redis Lua for atomic check-and-consume.

gotchas.trap: Adding a new algorithm by editing RateLimiter call sites or a giant math switch in the facade.
gotchas.correction: New class implementing Strategy plus one Factory branch; zero edits to RateLimiter callers.
Draw the 2× burst at the window edge; fix with sliding counter/log or switch to token bucket.

gotchas.trap: Claiming multi-pod correctness with only local in-memory maps.
gotchas.correction: Shared Redis with atomic Lua for token bucket; discuss fail-open vs fail-closed.

gotchas.trap: Memory grows forever as clients accumulate.
gotchas.correction: TTL/idle eviction on keys; Sliding Log is the worst offender versus token bucket or sliding counter.

gotchas.trap: Hardcoding free vs pro rates inside the strategy.
gotchas.correction: Use LimitResolver or config per plan so strategies stay pure rate math.

gotchas.trap: Background refill thread plus Thread.sleep in tests.
gotchas.correction: Prefer lazy refill on request plus injected Clock/FakeClock so tests advance time without sleeping.

gotchas.trap: Locking the entire ConcurrentHashMap or RateLimiter facade.
gotchas.correction: Correct but fails the concurrency follow-up—lock the per-key bucket, not the whole map.

gotchas.trap: Shipping only HLD Redis boxes when the round is LLD.
gotchas.correction: Draw classes and a working allow() first; Redis is stretch after the in-memory design.
